blindSourceSummaries: An international LGBT-rights organisation's country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex marriage and adoption legal since March 2022; hate-crime law aggravating SOGI motives since 2012; civil unions since 2015; self-determined legal gender recognition since 2019; third-sex birth option for intersex children since 2006; no statutory ban on medically unnecessary intersex surgeries (2023 health-ministry guidance is non-binding); the country's first lesbophobic-femicide conviction (2025, under a penal-code provision that aggravates killings motivated by sexual orientation, gender identity or expression); broad positive societal opinion but trans-rights pushback echoed by a recent parliamentary commission on trans minors (reported May 2025) recommending a ban on hormonal treatment for minors and audits of gender-affirming programmes; the national gender-identity support programme was excluded from the 2026 budget; concern over the 2025 presidential victory of a politician in an anti-marriage-equality network.
